newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Coromandel emergency seen lifted by noon - Radio NZ.
newsitem.headline: Coromandel emergency seen lifted by noon - Radio NZ.

text.p: A state of emergency in the Coromandel Peninsula was expected to be lifted by noon in the wake of Monday's storm, Radio New Zealand reported.
The Peninsula was the worst hit as the remnants of Cyclone Fergus swept down the east coast of the North Island and most of it remains cut off due to slips and flooding.
Hauraki Mayor Basil Morrison said the emergency committee would meet at nine o'clock and he hoped the state of emergency would be lifted this morning.
Huge slips on the Coromandel were still blocking roads, and holidaymakers trying to leave the area were queuing at road blocks.
At the Kopu Hikiwai turnoff, about 18 km north of Whangamata, two large fallen trees and stretches of knee-deep flooding had blocked the road.
Some boats had also broken their moorings in 70 km/hour winds, Radio NZ said. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
